key_insight: NAQsim is an open-source, full-stack simulation framework that reveals and helps eliminate hidden bottlenecks in neutral-atom fault-tolerant quantum computing, with patch rotations emerging as a major target for optimization.
engineering_relevance: It gives architects a practical tool to compare software, classical control, and device-level design choices for neutral-atom FTQC, enabling faster and more space-efficient transversal-surface-code systems.
method: Builds a detailed full-stack simulator for neutral-atom FTQC architectures based on transversal gates
Evaluates architecture choices across software, classical hardware, and quantum device layers
Uses the framework to co-optimize a near-rotation-free design (D3-ROT)
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that D3-ROT achieves a 2.27× speedup on practical FTQC benchmark workloads with minimal footprint overhead.
watch_item: Results come from a specific neutral-atom transversal-gate setting, so performance gains may not transfer directly to other hardware platforms or non-transversal architectures without re-evaluation.
paper_title: NAQsim: Full-Stack Architecture Simulation Framework for Fast and Space-Efficient Neutral Atom Quantum Computing
